newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat say early '97 results above forecast.
newsitem.headline: Fiat say early '97 results above forecast.

text.p: Italian industrial giant Fiat SpA said Thursday the company's results beat forecasts in the first few months of 1997.
Fiat said in a brief statement released after a board meeting that data for the first few months of the year showed "a positive trend and higher than the forecasts in the budget."
The Turin-based automaker also said the board had "examined a new forecast regarding the whole of 1997, the data for which will be illustrated at the shareholders' meeting on June 16."

It gave no other details but Fiat Chairman Cesare Romiti said last month that the company's 1997 sales would be around 90 trillion lire ($53 billion) compared with 78 trillion ($46 billion) in 1996, with profits forecast not below last year's.
Fiat made a consolidated net profit of 2.4 trillion ($1.4 billion) in 1996 and first quarter 1997 group sales rose 4.4 percent to 20.8 trillion ($11.9 billion).
Analysts said Fiat's revenues have been helped by a new incentive plan introduced by the Italian government at the start of this year to boost demand in the flagging sector.
Under the plan owners of cars more than 10 years old can receive a discount if they trade in old models for new cars. The plan is set to run through September.
